::: {#sol-deep-plain}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
plain_grad = first_layer_grad(make_deep())
plain_loss, plain_acc = train(make_deep())
print(plain_grad, plain_loss, plain_acc)
```

`r if (py$plain_loss > 0.9 * log(10)) "No" else "Yes"`.
Its training loss after 5 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$plain_loss)`,
against $\log 10 \approx `r sprintf("%.3f", log(10))`$ for probabilities of $\frac{1}{10}$,
and it classifies `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$plain_acc)`% of the test images correctly.
The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) that reaches its first layer has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_grad)`:
a [vanishing gradient](backpropagation.qmd#def-vanishing-gradient).
